items.summary: According to people familiar with the matter, Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei is vacationing at a luxury resort in southern Italy following the company's initial public offering. His private jet landed in Brindisi on Italy's Adriatic coast midday on Nov 20; local broadcaster Antenna Sud filmed him at the airport while Bloomberg News independently confirmed his arrival, and he was expected to stay for a few days. The sources spoke anonymously about these private matters, and Anthropic declined to comment. Amodei had made its Wall Street debut on Nov 19 after raising US$107.3 billion in a record-breaking public offering; shares soared 17% above their IPO price on the first day of trading but erased most of those gains on Nov 20, reflecting growing caution about the artificial intelligence trade. Brindisi is a historic port in Puglia, the region forming the heel of Italy's boot. Amodei has previously said he and his wife sometimes visit Italy, where they have a horse named Calypso.
items.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei vacations at Italian resort after public listing

items.summary: The article reports that Bitcoin fell to its lowest level in over two years, dropping 6% in the US on Nov 20 and another 5.7% in Asia on Nov 21 to reach US$55,533, which is described as its weakest point since September 2024. The article frames this decline within a broader market retreat from speculative bets following Donald Trump's re-election, noting that Bitcoin has lost more than half its value since peaking above US$126,000 in October 2025 and is now worth less than when crypto-friendly policies took effect. Multiple pressures are cited as contributing factors: a Binance hack at the end of October, Democratic midterm victories raising concerns about regulatory momentum, year-to-date ETF outflows exceeding US$3 billion (S$3.9 billion) amid an unraveling AI trade, and expectations of more aggressive Federal Reserve rate increases combined with a stronger dollar. The article attributes the speed of the decline to leverage, noting that Bitcoin's slide triggered roughly US$2 billion in long crypto liquidations over 24 hours on Nov 20, including US$94.6 million in BTC liquidations across Binance, Bybit, and OKX within an hour after Bitcoin broke below US$60,000. The piece contrasts this downturn with earlier crashes that featured forced selling or spectacular failures, describing the current decline as a steadier erosion of demand even though institutional acceptance has continued to advance.
items.title: Bitcoin falls to more than two-year low as global markets sink

items.summary: Professor Dame Henrietta Moore argues that AI raises a hidden "cognitive tax" by increasing cognitive load for the lowest-paid workers, who already face unpredictable pay, insecure housing and mounting debt. She contends that while employers increasingly value human judgment—according to the World Economic Forum, 59 in every 100 workers will need training to adapt by [d1: 2030]—automation also makes work less predictable through shifting schedules and adds mental fatigue from overseeing AI tools, straining minds already occupied by financial worries. Supporting evidence includes a 2024 analysis of [q4: 112,000 people] in the Journal of Economic Psychology showing that low-paid workers paid early were [q5: 7%] more productive and made fewer mistakes, and South African research finding men who retired at [q6: 60] rather than [q7: 65] showed slower memory decline. Moore also cites UK figures suggesting people facing insecurity across several life areas carry an earnings penalty as large as the gender pay gap that roughly doubles after seven years, and notes a Sam Altman-funded study found mental health gains from $1,000 monthly payments faded after one year—underscoring her view that universal basic services are needed. She calls on Britain's G20 presidency to require governments to assess how fiscal policies affect the cognitive load of the poorest people they touch.
items.title: AI's 'cognitive tax' falls hardest on low-paid workers

items.summary: The Global Energy Storage Alliance (GESA) launched on Nov. 13 inside the China Pavilion at COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, uniting 27 co-initiating organizations from battery manufacturers, power utilities, state-owned enterprises, and research institutions across China and other countries. The three founding bodies are the China Energy Storage Alliance, the China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute, and China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage Co., while the broader co-initiator roster includes CATL, BYD Energy Storage, EVE Energy, Hithium, Sungrow, CGN Energy International, POWERCHINA International, and Saudi Arabia's ACWA Power. Seven organizations — including the Long Duration Energy Storage Council, the International Hydropower Association, Energy Storage Europe, and the World Resources Institute — are listed as interested in exploring participation. The launch drew Chinese climate envoy Liu Zhenmin, IRENA Director-General Francesco La Camera, UN ESCAP Executive Secretary Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, and China's National Energy Administration Deputy Director-General Xiong Minfeng. GESA's founding declaration targets six focus areas: international dialogue; a global storage project and standards database; research and technology deployment; market mechanisms; supply chains and trade; and investment for developing economies — with the initiative positioning itself as open, technology-neutral, and respectful of differing national regulatory models. Sun Liqun of China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage framed three structural barriers: inadequate market mechanisms to value short- and long-duration storage, fragmented technical standards and regulations across countries, and financing and development obstacles in emerging economies; however, the text notes that how far a voluntary alliance can move these issues depends on engagement beyond the launch. The alliance also carries weight within UN climate processes by supporting efforts to triple renewable capacity by 2030 and directing South-South cooperation toward Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Latin America — regions where financing costs remain the largest deployment barrier — while for China it signals a shift from exporting storage products toward shaping global standards. The report is attributed to ESS News, and its assessment of GESA's potential impact remains qualified by uncertainty over future participation and engagement.
items.title: CATL, BYD, ACWA among co-initiators of storage alliance unveiled at COP31

items.summary: On International Men's Day, Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) published a reflection celebrating men across solar and energy transition industries who mentor, sponsor talent, challenge stereotypes, and help build an inclusive workplace. The piece frames gender equality as expanding opportunity rather than competition, drawing on contributions from Antonio Arruebo of SolarPower Europe ('Gender equality liberates everyone'), Emiliano Bellini of pv magazine (advocating tolerance for mistakes when addressing bias), Josef Kastner of Nexun (who challenged inappropriate behaviour toward a female manager and stated 'Everyone deserves the same rights and opportunities'), Frank Niendorf of JinkoSolar, Kim Keats of Ekon Strategy Consulting ('Our industry is ultimately about people...'), and Jesús Alijarde of Ibersyd/Cerfo. It links these ideas to Movember's focus on men's mental health and argues that inclusive cultures are shaped by what leaders tolerate and challenge. The article promotes Solar+ Leaders, WiSEu's gender-open leadership development ecosystem built around mentoring and shared learning, while noting the views expressed are those of the author rather than pv magazine.
items.title: Women in Solar+ Europe Celebrates Men on International Men's Day

items.summary: Waaree Forever Energies Private Limited, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Waaree Energies Limited, signed a Power Purchase Agreement with the Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited to develop a large-scale solar power and energy storage project in Solapur, Maharashtra. The PPA was executed on November 20, 2026, following an earlier intimation issued on August 28, 2026, and disclosed under Regulation 30 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015. The project combines 700 MW of solar power generation capacity with a 700 MW/2,800 MWh Energy Storage Solution designed to store energy generated during strong sunlight for use when solar output is low or unavailable, thereby supporting more reliable electricity supply and grid flexibility amid the intermittent nature of renewable sources. The agreement represents a significant addition to Maharashtra's planned renewable energy capacity but does not include disclosed details on development schedule, commissioning timeline, or tariff structure; it establishes only a formal contractual step toward developing the project.
items.title: Waaree Forever Signs PPA With SECI for 700 MW Solar and 2,800 MWh Storage Project in Maharashtra

items.summary: During the festive season, Hoymiles India's team visited Setu Foundation to share sweets and spend time with children supported by the organization. The visit coincided with a company message linking community engagement to its 'Open Energy for All' initiative, which it framed as being about people as much as power. Monika Shekhar, Deputy General Manager of Marketing at Hoymiles India, stated that the team would continue seeking ways to give back to surrounding communities and described happiness like energy as best when shared. Setu Foundation works with children and underserved communities across education, healthcare, and skill development programs aimed at improving access to opportunities; however, the text provides no specific details on program scale, funding amounts, or measurable outcomes from this visit.
items.title: Hoymiles India Visits Setu Foundation During Festive Season

items.summary: Building on a 2024 collaboration, DNV, an independent assurance provider, and PLN Enjiniring, a subsidiary of Indonesia's state-owned PT PLN (Persero), signed a new two-year Memorandum of Understanding to broaden their cooperation in supporting Indonesia's power system modernisation and energy transition. The companies plan to expand the scope of services across consultancy and engineering solutions 'to support the continued development, reliability, and long-term sustainability of Indonesia's power system,' combining PLN Enjiniring's local knowledge with DNV's international technical expertise. Their prior collaboration has delivered planning and advisory services across the sector as electricity demand grows and renewable energy develops, though this transition requires greater system flexibility to integrate variable renewables while maintaining reliable supply. Over the two-year framework, the partnership will jointly explore digital transformation and engineering initiatives through a Jakarta-based team working alongside PLN Enjiniring's engineers; DNV VP Lena Landsmann stated that 'Indonesia's energy transition depends not only on adding more renewable generation, but also on building the networks that can integrate it reliably.' The text presents these plans as intentions rather than completed work. No specific projects, funding figures, or measurable outcomes are reported.
items.title: DNV and PLN Engineering expand Indonesian power-sector partnership

items.summary: The article reports that Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang resigned from the company on [q1: 12] November after a dispute centered not primarily on an alleged affair but on the board's distrust of him for allegedly withholding full information. According to Wired, some members of the board objected more to his failure to tell the complete truth than to his private relationships with Alice Huang, who faces allegations of ties to Chinese intelligence agencies that China's foreign ministry has denied. The conflict reportedly began in [d1: 2025] October when questions arose about Nvidia's business dealings with Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, where Alice Huang had worked; the board asked Jensen about her but he allegedly denied improper connections. On [q2: 8] November, Jensen admitted to an affair with Alice and that same day announced an independent investigation, which was followed four days later by his resignation as CEO on [q3: 12] November. In a meeting with employees on [q4: 18] November, board chairman Harvey Jones said accepting the resignation had not been easy but cited concerns about honesty and trust in leadership after undisclosed personal conduct raised questions about the company's code of conduct and values. Despite his departure, calls for his return persist: President Donald Trump defended him as highly talented despite some poor decisions and urged Nvidia to let him apologize and return; reports also indicate that Elon Musk, thousands of employees, and some board members support reinstatement, with Jensen himself saying returning would be an honor. However, the article notes that on [q5: 17] November the Nvidia board stated it has no intention of making Jensen CEO again, leaving his eventual return uncertain while the company faces challenges around leadership stability and resolving investigation-related questions.
items.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns as CEO amid board distrust over withheld information and alleged affair with Alice Huang; Trump and Musk back his return, but Nvidia's board rejects it.

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India has clarified that resident individuals exporting services—such as freelancers, independent consultants, and other people receiving payments from overseas clients—are not required to separately file an Export Declaration Form (EDF) when accepting foreign remittances. This simplification appears in the RBI's frequently asked questions on the Foreign Exchange Management (Export and Import of Goods and Services) Regulations, 2026, which took effect on October 1. The central bank did not provide specific figures or additional details beyond this exemption clarification.
items.title: RBI exempts freelancers from separate export declaration filing

items.summary: The Telegraph's newsroom has become a site of leadership speculation and staff anxiety five months into its acquisition by German media company Axel Springer. Deputy editor Rob Winnett departed for the Daily Mail as chief content editor, but his exit is being read less as an ordinary reshuffle than as evidence that the title lacks direction under new owners who arrived with promises of investment yet appear focused on cost-cutting rather than expansion. Insiders report vague savings targets imposed on editor Chris Evans and no discernible long-term strategy, even though the company remains profitable; media analyst Alex DeGroote notes the redundancies are not driven by financial pressure but suggest a deep strategic rethink centered on AI. Axel Springer's chief executive Mathias Döpfner—who has pursued acquisitions such as Business Insider and Politico—has yet to clarify what role he intends for the Telegraph, leaving staff uncertain about their place in his plans amid questions raised at a town hall meeting with new CEO Carolin Hulshoff Pol about how AI will be used and why cuts continue despite healthy margins. These claims are drawn from unnamed sources and insider accounts within the newsroom; the reported political shift toward centre-right is attributed to some staff rather than confirmed by Axel Springer, and Döpfner's broader intentions remain speculative based on his past bids and reported interest in TikTok's European operations.
items.title: Telegraph departures signal concerns over direction under Axel Springer’s ownership

items.summary: Vincent Geloso's book, subtitled 'A New History of American Growth and Inequality, 1865-1945,' argues that the Gilded Age and Progressive Era saw far greater improvement in living standards than commonly acknowledged. From 1870 to just before World War I (the source text reads [q5: 191]), America experienced what Geloso calls 'the fastest and most stunning rise in the quality of life' ever recorded up to that point, benefiting especially the poorest 90% of Americans ([q1]). The period from World War I to the end of World War II brought slower but still substantial gains for those at the bottom. During these four decades (1870-191), living standards improved faster among the poorest [q2] than among the top 10 percent and as fast as among the top 1 percent ([q3], [q4]), which Geloso characterizes as a 'lean and mean egalitarian growth machine.' He attributes this dynamism primarily to America's market economy, which enabled people to relocate for better opportunities in industry or geography; while some government actions helped, he contends that market forces accounted for the lion's share of progress. Finally, Geloso argues that the American welfare state developed only after World War I because growth had slowed.
items.title: The Great Enrichment: A New History of American Growth and Inequality (1865-1945)

items.summary: On Nov 21, South Korean President Lee Jae-myung toured a data centre under construction in the southeastern city of Ulsan and urged the country to move quickly as it competes in the global artificial intelligence (AI) race. In a public video of the tour, he said 'The whole world is competing right now, and speed is vital.' Data centres are described as a major source of chip demand, and Lee hoped that this project's success would draw further investment from global AI companies; the facility was built by SK Group, South Korea's second-largest conglomerate. The Ulsan data centre is being developed jointly with Amazon Web Services (AWS), with an estimated cost of 7 trillion won (US$5.2 billion) until 2029 according to South Korea's science ministry, and operations are scheduled to begin in the second half of 2027. SK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won said in September that the capacity under construction was an initial 103 megawatt by 2029, with plans to expand it by nearly 900 megawatts in the future; he also noted the group is planning further partnerships with global technology companies as the project progresses. Lee observed that AI investment had mainly been concentrated around Seoul and said the Ulsan project showed regional growth was possible. After being told about 900 people were working at the site, he remarked that advanced facilities are short of construction workers and that ministries need to consider how to train the workforce for building data centres and AI infrastructure.
items.title: South Korea's Lee stresses speed in AI race during Ulsan data centre visit

items.summary: Rockstar Games reported that Grand Theft Auto VI generated $3.79bn in retail sales during its first day, which the company described as a new record for any entertainment product across all media. The worldwide figure reflects Rockstar's estimates through the end of Thursday, when the game launched on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S, debuting in New Zealand before rolling out market by market at midnight local time. Rockstar also said it had sold 32.5m units during prerelease, a record across platforms. The company framed these numbers as entertainment's biggest launch ever, though the figures are estimates rather than audited totals and reflect only first-day retail sales plus prerelease volume. For context, the figure is nearly five times the roughly $800m that Grand Theft Auto V attracted in its first 24 hours during its 2013 release, and it exceeds Avengers: Endgame's total box office run of about $2.9bn worldwide after a rerelease pushed it past Avatar as the highest-grossing film ever. The game received critical acclaim with a Metacritic score of 99, which Rockstar cited as making it the highest-rated game ever, though this is based on aggregated critic scores rather than independent verification.
items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI sets entertainment sales record on first day of release

items.summary: According to two people familiar with the matter, CrowdStrike is in ongoing negotiations to acquire rival cybersecurity provider Zscaler as enterprise customers increasingly favor consolidated security vendors. The discussions are not guaranteed and could end without an agreement. On Friday's close, Zscaler had a market capitalization of about $32 billion; its shares jumped 17 per cent in after-hours trading while CrowdStrike shares fell 8 per cent on the news. A combination would create one of the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity providers as companies seek to reduce their number of security vendors. CrowdStrike, founded in 2011 by George Kurtz and based in Austin, Texas, uses its Falcon platform for endpoint protection but has expanded into cloud, identity, and threat intelligence; the deal would address a gap in network security and help it compete with providers such as Palo Alto Networks. Zscaler, founded in 2007 by Jay Chaudhry, specializes in zero-trust, cloud-based network security that lets users access applications without traditional corporate networks. Any transaction would likely require backing from Chaudhry, who remains the largest shareholder. Bloomberg News first reported on the merger discussion.
items.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler amid cybersecurity sector consolidation

items.summary: Reed argues that skepticism of the AI trade is building, even as Anthropic's initial public offering proceeded well. The debut rose 17% over its initial price with a valuation of about $1.3 trillion, making it the biggest debut in history; yet shares fell 11% by midday and the broader market declined alongside them. Reed suggests some tech-industry observers would welcome a slowdown because resources are being concentrated among a small number of companies building essentially identical products, leaving little room for other ideas. He attributes this to an earlier 'tokenmaxxing' craze that accelerated revenue growth at frontier labs and hyperscalers but funnels every unit of memory and accelerator toward just a handful of players, which he says slows both innovation and AI adoption; these claims are drawn from his own experience with tech companies as well as a report by Wasabi and the Centre for Economics and Business Research. He also flags Jensen Huang's departure from Nvidia as bad news for pro-innovation advocates: Huang championed open-weight models and a healthy startup ecosystem, and such models—many originating in China—had helped seed wider AI adoption that could slow if Chinese firms cannot access enough Nvidia chips. A further drag on development is the growing number of cybersecurity concerns worldwide, since AI boosts productivity for threat actors and hostile nation states as well as legitimate users. Reed concludes that while growth may still favor large tech players, real-world impacts of AI are increasingly expected to take longer than initially anticipated.
items.title: Anthropic's record IPO gives way to a cooling AI market

items.summary: Levent Alpoge, a researcher at AI company Anthropic, stated Friday that he believes he has discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis using the firm's Claude chatbot. The hypothesis was first proposed by German mathematician Bernhard Riemann in 1859 and concerns the distribution of prime numbers; it is widely regarded as one of the most important open questions in pure mathematics, having eluded mathematicians for more than 160 years. Alpoge presented his claim in a four-page note released Friday. The text treats this assertion as an unverified statement from its source rather than established fact, noting no independent confirmation or details about the proof's validity are provided.
items.title: Anthropic Researcher Claims Claude Helped Prove Riemann Hypothesis

items.summary: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting adopted the APEC Connectivity Blueprint on Thursday, setting out priorities for strengthening Asia-Pacific links through infrastructure, institutional cooperation, and people-to-people exchanges. Its physical connectivity pillar encourages economies to develop reliable, scalable, trusted, secure, and resilient communication infrastructure; extend networks to rural and remote areas; enable next-generation technologies including low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites; and promote safe autonomous and unmanned transport through voluntary best-practice sharing. China's satellite efforts include two planned 10,000-satellite-class constellations—Guowang and Qianfan—with the country having carried out 80 space launches this year, nearly one-third of which involved satellite internet deployment; it also installed lightweight backup satellite base stations in Yunnan to maintain communications when ground cables are damaged. In digital transport, more than 70% of new passenger cars sold in China were equipped with Level 2 combined driver-assistance functions as of the October 2026 World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference, while Level 3 conditional automated-driving models entered road trials; MIIT reports that 57,000 kilometers of roads are open for testing and cumulative test mileage exceeded 220 million kilometers. The Ministry of Transport notes over 80,000 kilometers of trunk roads have undergone digital upgrades and more than 30,000 kilometers opened for autonomous-driving tests, with Sinotruk's intelligent trucks exceeding 100 million operating kilometers; in July, JD Logistics, Sinotruk, and Inceptio Technology launched the express delivery industry's first Level 4 autonomous heavy-truck freight demonstration project within Beijing. Senior officials will discuss implementation progress once a year from 2027 to 2030.
items.title: APEC adopts connectivity blueprint as China advances satellite and autonomous-driving programs

items.summary: Papua New Guinea announced in July 2025 that it would close a Taipei economic office, reflecting its adherence to the one-China principle and posing another challenge to Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities' efforts to expand Taiwan's so-called 'international space,' according to Prime Minister James Marape via a Xinhua report on November 12. Two commentaries published on Huanqiu.com criticized the DPP for pursuing international recognition through overseas offices, financial assistance, and high-profile events while questioning whether these efforts benefit Taiwanese residents or primarily serve the party's political agenda. One commentary cited July 2025 when South Africa requested that Taiwan's representative office change its name and relocate from Pretoria, February 2026 when Lithuania's prime minister acknowledged allowing a 'Taiwan'-named office had been a strategic mistake, and the DPP failing to secure an invitation to the World Health Assembly for the 10th consecutive year in May. Despite these setbacks, financial assistance to Palau reportedly increased from $18 million last year to $25 million this year, with additional funding pledged to Eswatini. Another commentary focused on the World Disaster Management Alliance established in September, noting only Taiwan's 11 remaining official partners and Somaliland agreed to join despite DPP promotion efforts. The commentaries argued that true international influence stems from economic strength, shared development, and practical cooperation rather than buying support or self-promotion, concluding that the DPP cannot bypass the one-China principle consensus.
items.title: DPP's overseas outreach faces setbacks amid one-China principle challenges

items.summary: The Schiller Think Tank UN Representative Richard Allen Black discussed a tripartite summit bringing together the heads of state of China, Russia, and the United States at APEC this week. The source frames the meeting as groundbreaking and describes it as forming 'a new kind of trust,' but offers no specific details about what was agreed or any measurable outcomes. Because the text contains only promotional framing without verifiable claims or data, a grounded summary is limited to identifying the event itself; there are no figures, dates, or comparable readings to support a chart.
items.title: APEC: Tripartite Summit of China, Russia, and United States Heads of State

items.summary: Negotiations at COP31 in Turkey ended in deadlock after countries could not agree on a new global climate deal, with the disagreement centered on whether to include any reference to reducing demand for fossil fuels. A group led by France and Panama pushed back against the draft agreement's omission of such language, arguing that an accord without mention of its cause was unacceptable; they also criticized references to carbon capture as effectively permitting continued oil and gas burning while claiming progress toward a 1.5C temperature target. The Africa Group separately demanded commitments for adaptation financing, noting that earlier proposals had included raising funding to $120bn by 2035 before it was removed from the text; Ghana's Environment Minister Zanetor Agyeman Rawlings framed this as claiming rights rather than begging. For the first time at a COP, the agreement—officially named the Antalya Accords—acknowledges that keeping global temperature rise below 1.5C has been missed and describes an ongoing period of "overshoot." Australia's climate change minister Chris Bowen countered by arguing the summit should focus on implementation and clean energy rather than fossil fuels; he cited reports that solar panels contributed the largest share of global energy demand growth this year, surpassing oil and gas for the first time. Separately, US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin agreed in Shenzhen to increase oil production amid fuel supply disruption from Iran War-related interruptions at the Strait of Hormuz; one proposal under discussion would keep fossil fuels off the table in exchange for petro-states pledging 35% of energy consumption to come from electricity by 2035. A new and potentially final agreement is expected Saturday, though climate activists have condemned the talks as "the worst COP ever," partly due to Turkey's lead negotiator walking out.
items.title: COP31 climate talks in deadlock over fossil fuel language

items.summary: US media report, citing two people briefed on the matter, that the FBI is investigating an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) database, which federal and local law enforcement use to share information on warrants and background checks. The BBC has contacted the FBI for comment but no official confirmation was provided in the reporting. This investigation follows a string of tech outages across banking, air traffic control, and other sectors last week that officials said were not caused by cyberattacks yet drew scrutiny from lawmakers. It also comes after White House National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross was fired this week amid criticism from President Donald Trump. The FBI has previously been targeted: in September it reported investigating a breach by the cyber-crime group ShinyHunters, which claimed to have stolen sensitive information on all bureau staff—around 38,000 people—and one former agent expressed concern for current employees' safety as personal data could become available online. Separately, NBC reported an apparent cyberattack against the US Department of Agriculture's farm payment system, though USDA has not publicly commented.
items.title: FBI investigating apparent hack of its criminal database

items.summary: At least [q3: 11 people] have died and more than [q4: 180] have been hospitalised after consuming suspected tainted liquor in Manipur's northeastern state of India. Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh announced the figures on Friday (Nov 20), noting that over [q5: 180 patients] had been admitted to two hospitals while the death toll reached [q6: 11] within the preceding 48 hours, and he ordered an enquiry with arrests promised for those responsible. The incident reflects a recurring pattern of deaths from illicit or adulterated alcohol in India, where cheap liquor sold outside regulated channels can contain methanol, a highly toxic industrial chemical that causes blindness, liver damage, and death at higher concentrations; the state's Chief Minister framed this event as part of that ongoing problem rather than an isolated occurrence. Comparable cases cited include May deaths from methanol-laced illicit liquor in Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad (Maharashtra), where [q7: 15 people] died, and August deaths in Gujarat's Bhavnagar district after consuming methanol-tainted liquor, affecting over [q8: 60]. The figures are drawn from the Chief Minister's statement on Friday; broader context about illicit alcohol consumption across India is attributed to local media reports.
items.title: 11 dead, over 180 hospitalised after drinking illicit alcohol in India

items.summary: U.N.-backed talks in Geneva produced a softened agreement to extend discussions on lethal autonomous weapons systems by two years, with nations agreeing only to elaborate a possible accord rather than commit to binding rules. The week-long conference ended Saturday without the legally binding deal sought by Secretary-General António Guterres, many countries, and activists. Izumi Nakamitsu hailed it as a significant achievement while acknowledging an ambiguous outcome against Guterres' hopes for a firm agreement this year. Activists blamed military powers like Russia and the United States for blocking stronger language; Stop Killer Robots called it a watered-down mandate and Lex International's Beatrice Fihn described pushing progress down the road by two years, with MIT's Max Tegmark noting states agreed to talk about the issue for the 14th year. Before the meeting, seven countries—Brazil, Austria, Belgium, Ireland, Mexico, New Zealand, and Panama—proposed launching negotiations on a rulebook that fell short. Guterres had set a 2026 deadline for starting such talks, while Pope Leo XIV and humanitarian groups framed the issue as existential. The Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons, ratified by 128 countries, requires consensus decisions, meaning any single country can thwart an agreement and deals are likely based on low common denominators.
items.title: UN Talks Yield Softened Agreement on AI Killer Robots, No Binding Rules

items.summary:
Prof Peter Hindmarsh, who gave expert evidence that helped convict Lucy Letby of murdering seven babies and attempting to murder a further seven — for which she is serving 15 whole-life sentences after refusing permission to appeal — was excluded by his employer UCLH from clinical practice in March 2023 because its medical director judged him unsafe advising children on insulin. The jury that convicted Letby five months later were never told of the exclusion, the GMC investigation (opened 25 November 2022), or a tribunal ruling.

In August 2023 Hindmarsh produced an expert report used by the CPS in the prosecution of Damion and Tamara Thomas over their son Joshua’s death from diabetic ketoacidosis on 10 December 2022. His report concluded it was not plausible there were no symptoms of diabetes, arguing medical help should have been sought earlier; Tamara was convicted of gross negligence manslaughter and neglect (sentenced to three years nine months) while Damion was found guilty only of neglect (two years nine months). Both parents maintain their innocence and are appealing.

Hindmarsh does not appear to have disclosed the GMC investigation or his exclusion to West Midlands police for more than two years, until he did so in December 2025 after being asked. The CPS independently discovered the restrictions in November 2025; it could not state how many prosecutions had relied on him while he was under investigation and decided it could continue using him as an expert.

The article notes that experts have a duty to disclose material undermining their credibility, including disciplinary proceedings, and raises questions over whether Hindmarsh complied. His barrister argued suspending his registration would be disproportionate given he could still work as an expert witness; the tribunal in April 2023 declined to suspend him but imposed stricter supervision.

The investigation never reached a final adjudication: Hindmarsh applied for voluntary erasure, granted in November 2024. His self-certificate disclosed only his lack of accreditation and did not mention UCLH’s concerns or the March 2023 exclusion; Alessandro Thomas said it was misleading to portray him as currently practising at UCLH.

The article is based on reporting by The Guardian, which declined to answer questions about Hindmarsh’s disclosure. West Midlands police stated its investigators fulfilled their obligations and made information available to the CPS in a timely manner as it became available; the CPS said it met all disclosure obligations and no objections were raised at any stage.
items.title: Letby trial expert witness barred from treating patients was used in another prosecution

items.summary: At a summit in Brussels, the UK and EU signed three agreements on Friday that aim to reduce red tape for food exports, link their emissions trading schemes, and allow tens of thousands of young people to live and work more freely across the Channel. These deals represent a renewed effort to reset post-Brexit relations between the two sides. Prime Minister Andy Burnham has framed Brexit as an 'obvious failure' to deliver on its promises and wants to deepen ties with the EU, though this position is being criticised by veteran Brexiteer Nigel Farage, who warns of a political backlash over the move.
items.title: EU and UK sign three agreements to reset post-Brexit relations

items.summary: In [d1: 2025], a Mongabay video team reported that Lundy, a rugged island in the Bristol Channel between Wales and England, has become one of the UK's most notable conservation success stories. Seabird numbers on the island rose from around [q1: 6000] two decades ago to approximately [q2: 48,000], driven by an eradication program begun in the early 2000s that removed rats preying on seabird burrows and chicks. The recovery has drawn thousands of visitors annually seeking species such as puffins and seals. In addition to terrestrial gains, Lundy's waters became the UK's first marine nature reserve, with its no-take zone established in [d1: 2003] through collaboration between local fishermen, conservationists, and business owners rather than imposed externally. Within this zone, fishing is prohibited except for recreational rod-and-line activities and lobster potting; trawling and dredging are banned. Fishermen report that lobsters inside the no-take zone can number as many as [q7: 75] per night versus roughly [q6: 12] outside it on a comparable string of pots, with studies indicating that lobsters there have grown both larger and more numerous while spilling over into neighboring grounds. The Marine Protected Area was created specifically to protect spiny lobsters brought back from near-extinction as well as slow-growing habitats such as pink sea fans, which trawling would destroy almost instantly. The video team noted the approach's success stems from broad local buy-in and that conservation has generated jobs while attracting visitors; they also flagged that balancing wildlife protection with human use remains an ongoing challenge into the future.
items.title: Lundy Island's seabird recovery and marine protection

items.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) unveiled on Saturday a revamped central contract structure effective for the 2026-27 season, expanding the contracted player pool from [q1: 30] to [q2: 38]. Salman Ali Agha and Babar Azam are the only players placed in the highest category. The new contracts run through June 30, 2027 ([d1]), ending a period during which players had been without central contracts since the previous cycle expired in June. Eligibility requires male cricketers to have played at least four tests, six one-day internationals, or six Twenty20s within the preceding 12 months (a rule announced in June). Contracts are now divided into five specialised categories: tests and ODIs, test specialists, ODIs and T20Is, T20I specialists, and emerging players in the developmental pathway. Notable omissions include former captain Mohammad Rizwan, former Test skipper Shan Masood, opener Saim Ayub, Hasan Ali, Abdullah Shafique, Mohammad Haris, Mohammad Nawaz, Noman Ali, Hussain Talat, Khurram Shahzad, Abbas Afridi, and Mohammad Wasim Jr.
items.title: Pakistan expands central contract pool to 38 players under new format-based system for 2026-27

items.summary: Despite public emphasis on securing better EU trade terms and reforming Britain's welfare system, Prime Minister Andy Burnham has privately been preoccupied with the trajectory of the Iran war. According to people familiar with the matter, Burnham and his most senior Cabinet colleagues have for several weeks focused on the possibility that Donald Trump could resume major strikes on Iran; while ministers had hoped the Republicans' midterm defeat might temper Trump's foreign policy, they see him weighing options for a fresh attack—a prospect said to have grown in recent days. On Friday, Burnham finalized an agreement for closer EU ties he described as potentially boosting the economy by 0.5% annually and lowering food and electricity prices; however, Iran remained looming in the background. Even if Trump chooses not to resume hostilities, officials reportedly told him that all plausible outcomes would negatively affect both the U.K.'s economy and security.
items.title: Burnham's Priority: Iran Over Brexit or Welfare

items.summary: The US Department of War published a new batch of declassified files on unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP), marking the eighth release under its government disclosure programme. The documents are accessible through PURSUE, the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters, hosted on the department's website. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell stated that the department and partner agencies were already preparing the next release, with additional files to be published on a rolling basis. This disclosure effort continues prior attempts to make historical records about unexplained phenomena publicly available.
items.title: Pentagon Releases Eighth Batch of Declassified UAP Files

items.summary: Chinese geologists announced on Friday that they have discovered rocks dating back 3.95 billion years, the oldest known in Asia and providing key evidence for understanding Earth's early evolution. The discovery was made by a team led by Wan Yusheng of the Chinese Academy of Geological Sciences, with samples found in the eastern part of Hebei Province, north China. Because geological records from Earth's first few hundred million years are extremely difficult to preserve, such 'childhood' period samples are very rare; these rocks were dated at 3.95 billion years. The findings indicate that some form of subduction-related tectonic activity may have occurred on Earth around this time and provide direct evidence that the mantle had already become depleted during the Hadean Eon. Previously, the world's oldest recognized rocks were the Acasta Gneiss in Canada, about 4 billion years old; this new discovery narrows the gap with the world record to just 50 million years while remaining the first such find in Asia. The findings have been published in the journal Nature.
items.title: Oldest Known Rocks in Asia Discovered in North China

items.summary:
COP31 climate negotiations in Antalya, Turkey have spilled into Saturday as countries race to secure a deal after a draft text removed all references to fossil fuels. A first version of the agreement had called for an accelerated phase-out of fossil fuels, but a second draft released Thursday dropped every mention of those energy sources, prompting pushback from nations including France and Panama. Negotiators from nearly 200 countries have struggled through deep divisions over both fossil fuels and climate finance at the conference. On Friday, several countries issued a letter insisting that any deal include "a clear transition away from fossil fuels," while the European Union warned the revised draft risked turning the talks into a "fossil summit." Panama threatened to walk away, with its environment minister Juan Carlos Navarro accusing a "petroleum mafia" of blocking progress. COP31 President and Turkish Environment Minister Murat Kurum told an assembly late Friday that negotiators were close but not finished, while Australian Climate Minister Chris Bowen said he would work as long as it takes to complete the agreement. A new deal is expected to be published Saturday. Separately, OPEC reported that its Secretary General Haitham al-Ghais met with Russian climate envoy Ruslan Edelgeriev at COP31 to discuss inclusive and balanced approaches across multilateral environmental forums.

items.summary: A US-French man was convicted by a federal jury in the US District Court for Los Angeles on arson charges tied to the January 1, 2025 brush fire that ignited in the Santa Monica Mountains National Recreation Area and grew into the destructive Palisades Fire. Prosecutors relied on security camera footage and cellphone location data showing he was the only person near the initial blaze; they described him as a former Uber driver who held resentment toward society and especially wealthy people, though he declined to testify at either trial. The fire killed 12 people and destroyed roughly 6,800 homes and other structures with estimated property losses of $150 billion (€136.7 billion). He was arrested in October 2025 after a prior trial ended in a hung jury that led to a June mistrial; prosecutors retried him under modified charges, and he is scheduled for sentencing on March 17, facing up to 40 years in prison. The defense contended the initial fire could have been caused by fireworks, which prosecutors said had no evidence of being set off.
items.title: Man Convicted of Arson in Deadly Los Angeles Palisades Fire

items.summary: On Friday, Haiti's government announced an agreement with El Salvador to build three new prisons in collaboration with a local company. The deal follows the deployment of 2,500 Salvadoran troops to help fight armed gangs who control some 70 per cent of Port-au-Prince and large parts of central Haiti; two soldiers were killed and two injured in an explosion while handling explosives at a camp. Haitian Justice Minister Patrick Pélissier made the announcement after visiting El Salvador, where he praised CECOT, its maximum security prison. The agreement comes as El Salvador has been under a state of exception since 2022 that has seen more than 90,000 people imprisoned without family visits, and Haiti's prisons have struggled with overcrowding after gangs raided the country's two largest prisons in 2024, releasing thousands. Pélissier said the prime minister had issued instructions to submit the project to relevant authorities to expedite it. He did not disclose how much the projects would cost, whether El Salvador would help finance them, or any management role for El Salvador.
items.title: Haiti and El Salvador Reach Prison-Building Agreement Amid Troop Deployment

items.summary: Former Australian cricket coach Darren Lehmann denied knowing of a specific conversation in which David Warner raised using sandpaper on the ball, as detailed by Cameron Bancroft earlier that week. He said he could not remember being present at such a discussion and attributed the difficulty to the event occurring eight and a half years prior. Lehmann acknowledged that his version differed from Bancroft's account of him contacting Peter Handscomb via walkie-talkie to have Bancroft remove sandpaper, stating instead that he only became aware of it after seeing footage on TV. He apologised for the team's culture during the 2018 South Africa tour, admitting attempts to achieve reverse swing "went too far" and describing his experience as a dark period from which recovery took three to four years; Lehmann also expressed empathy toward Bancroft and other players and staff while criticising doorstopping reporters. He denied intentionally avoiding questions about ball tampering but conceded the environment prioritised winning at all costs, and said he had no evidence supporting claims made by bowlers Pat Cummins, Mitchell Starc, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon, though he stated he trusted them. Lehmann confirmed he would attend Cricket Australia's independent forum on the tour to share his account, as have Cummins, Usman Khawaja, Warner and Bancroft.
items.title: Lehmann denies knowledge of 2018 sandpaper plan despite Bancroft statement

items.summary: About [q1: 24,000 properties] were without power Thursday during a mass blackout on the Eyre Peninsula. An intense storm damaged three transmission towers that operator ElectraNet said crippled the radial line powering much of the peninsula, including Port Lincoln; the company is investigating whether structural defects caused it but says this is unlikely and maintains its designs meet Australian standards. The mothballed, privately owned Port Lincoln power station—which will shut down permanently in [d1: 2028]—is temporarily servicing the region for several days while temporary structures are expected within days to improve reliability; there is still no timeline for permanent replacement of the damaged towers. Port Lincoln mayor Diana Mislov called the severe weather an unexpected event but urged construction requirements be met and wanted the plant maintained long-term as backup, also asking residents switch off solar panels per SA Police instructions. Premier Peter Malinauskas warned predicted Sunday storms and heat could further strain the grid; the Bureau of Meteorology forecasts early thunderstorms with temperatures reaching around [q2: 30] on the Lower Eyre Peninsula. Restaurant owner Craig McCathie said a multi-day blackout like in [d2: 2016] would be problematic if town reserves run out, noting his venue keeps about 20 hours of fuel but loses its back-up plan when diesel pumps go down.
items.title: Eyre Peninsula residents rely on temporary fixes after mass blackout leaves ~24,000 properties without power

items.summary: As China discards over 400 million smartphones annually, emerging markets in Africa and South Asia are increasingly sourcing refurbished devices from the country. Counterpoint Research reports that the global secondary smartphone market grew 13 per cent year-on-year in the first half of 2026 to 150 million units, driven by chip shortages and rising prices making new phones harder to afford abroad. Chinese buyers like Pakistani businessman Akhtar Muhammad purchase broken devices to export for repair, while Nigerian trader Mama reportedly bought around 40 used phones in a single day at Shenzhen's electronics markets, noting they are more expensive in Africa due to the absence of large suppliers. ATRenew operates PaiJiTang Mall near Shenzhen as a formalized self-service marketplace displaying over 20,000 used phones and drawing up to 1,000 visitors daily, with international traders making up about a third; Algerian shopkeeper Abdul Rahim flies there three times monthly to exploit a price gap of $110 to $132 per device. ATRenew's processing hub in Dongguan receives roughly 30,000 second-hand gadgets daily and is inspected by over 300 technicians before outbound shipments at similar volumes; Apple devices account for 70 to 80 per cent of sales, with the remainder split among Chinese brands. Counterpoint notes that older models like the iPhone 11, 12, and 13 are losing ground domestically but retain strong brand power overseas where they find a second life.
items.title: China's used smartphone trade expands to South Asia and Africa

items.summary: Mathieu Potte-Bonneville, a philosopher and professor at École Normale Supérieure de Lyon who directs the Department of Culture and Creation at Centre Pompidou, is regarded as one of the leading experts on Michel Foucault. He became interested in Foucault through his involvement in AIDS activism alongside Daniel Defert, Foucault's partner, after reading The Order of Discourse; he also co-authored an illustrated biography with cartoonist Morvandiau and wrote Foucault: The Restlessness of History. Speaking at the Centre de Cultura Contemporània de Barcelona ahead of a sold-out event on Foucault's contemporary relevance in 2026 — the centenary of his birth, following Foucault's death from AIDS-related complications in summer 1984 — Potte-Bonneville explained that Foucault remains highly cited because he never stopped publishing and because his work spans philosophy, history, literature and social sciences. He noted major influence on Judith Butler, Achille Mbembe and Gayatri Spivak, describing the era as a 'neo-Foucauldian moment' or 'Foucault 2.0.' Potte-Bonneville argued that Foucault's relevance lies not in prophecy but in analyzing how surveillance and power transform over time; he cited an AI tool called Foukenstein created in September, which simulates Foucault's voice while showing only a turtleneck sweater to illustrate the death of the author. He also pointed to high school students carrying a 'Discipline and Punish' banner at a recent Paris demonstration as evidence that Foucault's message has returned to current events. On resistance, Potte-Bonneville said Foucault was cautious about the term but interested in moments when power is checked while enabling something new; he cited the 2018 Yellow Vests movement as exemplifying this ambiguity and highlighting an invisible segment of French society living far from decision-making centers. He concluded that a key lesson is to abandon apocalyptic narratives, since Foucault's work largely omits the future — when asked about it, Foucault refused to answer, arguing instead for engaging in politics in the present.
items.title: Philosopher Mathieu Potte-Bonneville on Michel Foucault's enduring relevance

items.summary:
Danmei—stories of romance between two men written primarily by Chinese women—is a genre that has grown steadily over the past decade on China's digital platforms, fueling a thriving industry of screen adaptations including manhua, animated or live-action series, and audio dramas. The roots trace to Japanese Boys' Love manga from the 1970s, which spread to China in the 1990s following economic opening; local fans then began writing their own stories as internet access expanded. Spanish publisher Norma launched a dedicated danmei imprint in [d1: 2024], now releasing two new titles monthly and drawing on works by authors such as Mo Xiang Tong Xiu, whose output reportedly helped put the phenomenon on the global map. Readers are mostly women aged 18 to 40, though academic Qi Zhang disputes that readers are predominantly heterosexual, noting queer people make up a significant sector of the community. Censorship has shaped the genre: authorities have detained and fined authors—most publishing under pseudonyms—and Qi points to the government's [d2: 2014] anti-pornography campaign as a turning point when platform Jinjiang renamed its danmei section chun'ai ('pure love') and restricted sexual content. In [d3: 2024], more than [q1: 50 people] publishing on Haitang, an erotic-fiction platform hosted in Taiwan, were detained or fined; the most high-profile case was Yun Jian, sentenced to four and a half years for obscenity after earning about [q2: 1.85 million yuan] ([q3: $274,700]) from [q4: 37 novels]. In [d4: 2025], Reuters documented another wave of arrests under regulations prohibiting obscene material; some investigated had earned only a few thousand yuan. These pressures have led authors like Xu Ren to avoid unofficial channels and reconsider where they publish, with fears that exposure could jeopardize their professional futures.

visual limitations: The source data references are not directly comparable for charting—Norma's 2024 launch is an event rather than a measurement; the detentions count (50+) refers to people on Haitang in one year while Yun Jian's earnings and novel count describe her individually, making cross-chart comparison misleading. No single measure ties these figures together over time or across groups.
items.title: Chinese danmei novels reached global audiences despite censorship and author detentions.

items.summary: A magnitude 6.7 earthquake struck approximately 22 kilometers (14 miles) west-northwest of Ondores in central Peru's Junin region on Friday, according to the US Geological Survey. The agency initially reported the quake at magnitude 6.9 before revising it down to 6.7. It occurred at 7:09 pm local time (0009 GMT Saturday) at a depth of about 142.1 km (88 miles). The US National Tsunami Warning Center confirmed no tsunami warning, advisory, watch, or threat followed the event, and there were no immediate reports of casualties or significant damage.
items.title: Magnitude 6.7 Earthquake Strikes Peru's Junin Region

items.summary: An Indigenous-led conservation effort led by Maribel Pacco of the Pillco Grande Quechua community is documenting Andean bears (Tremarctos ornatus) using camera traps across Pumataki, a private cloud forest reserve in southeastern Peru. The team has identified 10 individual bears through their unique facial markings, providing some of the first local records of the species on the reserve and helping inform a Quechua-language environmental education program for youth. Pacco received funding from SPDA's Conservamos por Naturaleza grant to launch this initiative. Andean bears are listed as vulnerable by IUCN; Peru is considered one of their strongholds, with an estimated 5,000 individuals believed to roam the country. Pumataki lies in a buffer zone near Manu National Park and holds spiritual significance for local Quechua people. The project has also captured images of other species such as clouded oncilla, dwarf brocket deer, puma, opossums, and coatis. Despite limited funding forcing some plans to scale back, community members continue monitoring in groups of five while forming a management committee.
items.title: Quechua community in Peru builds up Andean bear camera trap project on their own reserve

items.summary: Following recent scandals involving two iconic British comedians, the UK government is considering introducing staggered age-of-consent laws that would set different ages for sexual activity with men and women. In a discussion featuring Annette Young interviewing Katherine Allen from the Institute of Social Justice in the UK, the program examines whether such staggered consent laws are effective at protecting young people. The episode also addresses related social issues: the social costs of femicide, how loved ones cope with losing someone to such violence, and what support is available to families affected by these tragedies. Additionally, it profiles women challenging the male-dominated traditions of Mexican mariachi music. No specific data or statistics are provided in the source text regarding consent law effectiveness or any other topic covered.
items.title: Does staggered consent actually protect young people?

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India clarified that companies and other non-individual service exporters must file an Export Declaration Form (EDF) only when a single overseas inward remittance exceeds Rs 10 lakh, with the threshold applied per individual payment. In FAQs published on November 20, RBI stated: “The EDF needs to be filed only by persons other than resident individuals in cases where the value of each inward remittance exceeds ₹10 lakh (or its equivalent in foreign currency).” Resident individuals—including freelancers and independent consultants—can instead supply their authorised dealer with payment details for crediting accounts; this form is deemed submitted regardless of amount. For non-individual exporters, the declaration must be filed before credit except for export advances, which require filing within 30 days from month-end following invoice issuance. A service export invoice raised before October 1 does not trigger a requirement even if payment arrives on or after that date. For imports, the Rs 10 lakh threshold applies to the invoice or contract value, so resident individuals and importers with invoices up to Rs 10 lakh can continue providing information their authorised dealers already seek. Authorised dealers must keep reporting remittances for both service exports and imports in RBI’s monitoring systems. The second amendment was notified on November 2 after stakeholder feedback and applied retrospectively from October 1, when the underlying trade regulations (issued January 13) took effect; RBI said the framework aims to promote ease of doing business for small exporters and importers and speed up authorised dealer service. The item is dated November 21, 2026.
items.title: RBI clarifies ₹10-lakh export declaration threshold applies to each service payment

items.summary: On November 21, 2026, Google announced it would provide the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur (IIT Kharagpur) with USD [q3: 5 million], about Rs [q2: 46 crore] to develop and accelerate advanced AI research. The announcement was made by IIT Kharagpur Director Suman Chakraborty on the institute's 75th anniversary, noting that the funding for applied AI research had been envisioned by Sundar Pichai, an alumnus of the institute and Google CEO. In a company blog, Google stated it would provide USD [q1: 5 million] in funding to help develop and accelerate advanced AI research while cultivating India's next generation of scientific and technical talent. The fund will support researchers and students across three core pillars—advanced AI research, educational opportunities, and AI capacity building—with the research pillar targeting real-world challenges through applications in Indic languages, materials science, agriculture, and educational technology; the education pillar supporting expansion of AI training and curriculum development for students and faculty; and the capacity-building pillar strengthening campus-wide AI frameworks and tooling. Pichai said India is increasingly at the forefront of innovation and that programmes like this would help implement Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of reaching everyone in India with the benefits of AI.
items.title: Google to fund IIT Kharagpur's advanced AI research with $5 million

items.summary: According to Bloomberg reports and an opinion piece by Dave Lee, Apple is shifting its AI strategy from embedding intelligence in existing products toward developing an autonomous agent that can browse the internet, operate applications, write and debug code, and execute multi-step tasks across browsers, terminals, editors, and services. The company signaled these plans through job listings for a senior engineering manager of a proactive agentic assistant capable of coordinating specialized subagents, though its recruitment activity suggests significant development work remains before any launch—possibly as soon as the end of next year. Apple is entering an already-established market: Meta's Muse ranks No. 2 among free applications on Apple's App Store (behind TikTok), with ChatGPT and Claude also in the top five; Anthropic has widened testing of Duet, OpenAI expanded Dots, and Google overhauled its agent into Tasks, which can now make phone calls for users. Coding tools like Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor further crowd the space. Apple's potential edge lies in its installed iPhone base, OS control, privacy reputation, and hardware portfolio (AirPods, Apple Watch), while third-party agents face restrictions—Meta's Muse cannot read text messages or Mail on iPhone—and macOS 27.3 beta raised the steps required to enable ChatGPT computer-use tools from four to 14. However, these changes are viewed by some as attempts to hinder competitors rather than purely security measures; Apple plans emphasize permission models and sandboxing for agents that run code or access credentials. The move could also invite regulatory scrutiny in Europe if its agent gains access rivals lack.
items.title: Apple's late entry into AI agents amid a crowded market

items.summary: Google announced a $5 million (approximately ₹46 crore) investment in the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Kharagpur to strengthen artificial intelligence research, expand education, and develop India's next generation of technology professionals. The funding coincides with the institute's 75th anniversary and was envisioned by Google CEO Sundar Pichai, an alumnus of the institution. Director Suman Chakraborty confirmed that the support for applied AI research reflects Pichai's vision, aiming to strengthen India's AI ecosystem through researchers, faculty, and students working on emerging technologies. The investment will focus on three major areas: advanced AI research across Indic languages, agriculture, materials science, and education technology; expansion of AI training programs and curriculum development; and support for AI frameworks, tools, and research infrastructure. Pichai emphasized that India is becoming a major innovation hub and expressed confidence the collaboration would create opportunities for future generations while advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of making AI benefits accessible to everyone.
items.title: Google Announces $5 Million AI Funding for IIT Kharagpur

According to monthly data from ACE MF for October, Indian mutual funds cut their aggregate cash allocation by nearly Rs 7,800 crore on a monthly basis to Rs 1.74 lakh crore, down from Rs 1.82 lakh crore in September. The industry's cash holdings represented 3.81% of total assets during the period, while equity AUM stood at Rs 45.79 lakh crore.

Six fund houses each held more than Rs 10,000 crore in cash: SBI Mutual Fund led with Rs 25,520 crore (3.36% of total assets) and an equity AUM of Rs 7.34 lakh crore; HDFC Mutual Fund followed with Rs 20,834 crore (4.29%) against a Rs 4.64 lakh crore equity AUM; PPFAS Mutual Fund held Rs 20,095 crore (13.12%) over a Rs 1.33 lakh crore equity AUM; ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund had Rs 16,713 crore (3.02%) with a Rs 5.36 lakh crore equity AUM; Axis Mutual Fund held Rs 12,437 crore (6.22%) over a Rs 1.87 lakh crore equity AUM; and Quant Mutual Fund had Rs 11,658 crore (13.24%) against a Rs 76,382 crore equity AUM.

PPFAS noted in its monthly release that it continues to assess individual investments on their own merits rather than relying heavily on the macroeconomic situation, and reported about 8.78% cash holdings alongside debt, money market instruments, and arbitrage positions available for deployment at appropriate levels. Fund managers generally retain a portion of portfolios in cash to meet redemption requests or deploy capital when attractive opportunities arise.

The figures are drawn from ACE MF data as compiled by ETMarkets.com; the article does not provide September-level detail for each individual fund house, so month-over-month changes cannot be calculated per AMC.
items.title: Six mutual funds held over Rs 10,000 crore in cash as industry holdings fell to Rs 1.74 lakh crore in October

items.summary: At IIT Kharagpur's Platinum Jubilee celebrations on November 21, Prime Minister Narendra Modi recounted skepticism raised about the semiconductor mission when he launched it in December 2021. He reported that critics questioned whether India needed to enter an industry other countries had already developed over decades of experience, and he responded by challenging them with the question 'Should India just sit idly by forever?' Modi characterized this doubt as a reflection of a limited mindset and said he worked directly with officials to prepare plans for the mission rather than accept that India had missed its opportunity. He cited progress since the initiative began, including semiconductor fabrication and packaging projects approved across the country, involvement of IIT Kharagpur alumni in those projects, and claims that India has begun exporting chips. Modi also extended his argument beyond industrial policy to individual thinking, describing limiting beliefs as self-imposed boundaries on one's dreams, talents, and a nation's potential, while arguing that accepting such limits prevents people from realizing their full capability.
items.title: Modi Defends India's Semiconductor Mission Against Critics

items.summary: Union home minister Amit Shah, visiting Arunachal Pradesh on Saturday amid protests against the proposed 11,200-MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), assured locals at a Police Training Centre in Banderdewa near Itanagar that the government would protect their traditions, culture and religious beliefs. His remarks marked his first public statement on the issue as he acknowledged some of the concerns raised were significant while urging residents to engage with the state government and convey grievances through the Union home ministry via local administration. The opposition comes primarily from indigenous Adi community members in Siang and Upper Siang districts, who cite possible impacts on ancestral lands, villages, livelihoods, environment and cultural identity, along with allegations of inadequate public consultation during the pre-feasibility report exercise. They also question the need for such a massive project given the fragile ecology of the Siang Valley and its seismically sensitive region. The Centre considers the river project strategically important in response to China's plans to develop hydropower on the upper reaches of the Yarlung Tsangpo River, which becomes the Brahmaputra after entering India as the Siang before flowing into Assam; it is expected to provide hydroelectric power while regulating flows and supporting revenue generation, infrastructure development and employment. The report draws on PTI inputs.
items.title: Amit Shah Assures Arunachal Locals of Dialogue Amid Siang Dam Protests

items.summary: Congress Rajya Sabha MP Ranjeet Ranjan called on fellow Congress MP Imran Masood to keep politics and sports separate after the latter questioned Mohammed Siraj's omission from India's Test squad. Ranjan argued that sports has its own selection criteria and politicians should not bring athletes into political discourse, urging them instead to let players be chosen based on merit and performance regardless of origin. The dispute arose when Masood alleged discrimination over Siraj being left out of the squad and subsequently raised Mohammed Shami and Sarfaraz Khan in connection with the discussion, questioning whether selection was fair. Ranjan's response framed his concern around maintaining a boundary between political involvement and sporting decisions rather than addressing the specifics of the selection process itself.
items.title: Congress MP Ranjeet Ranjan Urges Imran Masood to Keep Politics Separate from Sports

items.summary: In his book Searching for Alpha: The Quest for Exceptional Investment Performance, Ben Warwick argues that investors and fund managers can generate alpha—returns above a market benchmark—by identifying mispriced securities and exploiting market inefficiencies. He notes that consistently outperforming the broader market is difficult, with more than half of actively managed mutual funds historically failing to beat the S&P 500 (q1), and that funds which outperform in one year often struggle to repeat it later. Warwick attributes much of this difficulty to fund size: as assets under management grow, managers must hold a broader range of companies—often large-cap stocks with heavy analyst coverage—and larger transactions can move prices enough to erode gains from buying undervalued securities. He also points out that managers have an incentive to grow funds because their fees are typically tied to asset size. Despite these obstacles, Warwick believes active strategies such as arbitrage, frequent trading, options plays, and small-cap investments can still deliver superior returns—though smaller companies carry greater risk and may fall more sharply during downturns. He then outlines nine approaches: diversify across sectors rather than concentrating in a few stocks (treating Buffett and Keynes as exceptions); use index funds where markets are efficient; pursue active management in inefficient segments like small-caps and high-yield bonds; monitor credit spreads to gauge economic conditions; apply momentum investing during expansions while recognizing weak economies can undermine it; consider alternatives such as futures and market-neutral hedge funds for diversification; minimize taxes by using index funds in efficiently priced areas and placing active holdings in tax-deferred accounts; choose managers based on transaction costs, fees, and research budget rather than past performance alone; and rebalance regularly to exploit mean reversion. Warwick cautions that these strategies do not guarantee market-beating returns.
items.title: Ben Warwick's nine strategies for generating market-beating returns

items.summary: According to a report by SIF360, Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs) have seen rapid adoption since the launch of their regulatory framework. As of October 31, 2026, nearly 18 asset management companies offered SIFs and collectively managed Rs 42,669 crore in assets under management. Of these 18 SIFs, the top nine each hold more than Rs 1,000 crore AUM. Altiva SIF by Edelweiss Mutual Fund leads with the highest AUM of Rs 14,370 crore, followed by iSIF (ICICI Prudential) at Rs 6,465 crore, Magnum SIF (SBI) at Rs 5,684 crore, QSIF (Quant) at Rs 4,412 crore, Infinity SIF (Kotak) at Rs 3,841 crore, RedHex SIF (HSBC) at Rs 1,796 crore, Dyna SIF (360 One) at Rs 1,230 crore, and Titanium SIF (Tata) at Rs 1,209 crore. Apex SIF by Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund holds Rs 1,043 crore. The remaining nine SIFs — Prism, Summit, Platinum, Arudha, Diviniti, Sapphire, MSIF, Arthaya, and WSIF — have AUM ranging between Rs 123 crore and Rs 617 crore.
items.title: 18 AMCs Manage Rs 42,600 Crore Through SIFs in October; Top Nine Exceed Rs 1,000 Crore AUM

items.summary: According to the EdelGive Hurun India Philanthropy List 2026, released on November 20, India's wealthiest philanthropists donated ₹11,554 crore during fiscal year 2026, an 11% increase over last year's total contributions of ₹10,380 crore. The list features 219 donors and recorded 45 new entrants compared with the previous year. HCL Technologies founder Shiv Nadar retained his position as India's most generous philanthropist for a fifth consecutive year; he and his family donated ₹2,593 crore during FY26, which translates to around ₹7.1 crore every day despite a 4% annual decline. The gap between Nadar's donations and those of the second-ranked donor is described as a massive ₹1,716 crore. Gautam Adani and his family climbed three positions to secure 2nd place with contributions that surged 127%, reaching ₹877 crore from ₹386 crore last year; the Bajaj family retained 3rd position with donations worth ₹632 crore (increasing 42%), while Mukesh Ambani and his family ranked 4th contributing ₹620 crore. Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani secured 5th place with ₹380 crore, Kumar Mangalam Birla followed with ₹366 crore, Cyrus Poonawalla and Adar Poonawalla ranked 7th having donated ₹336 crore, Sudhir Mehta and Samir Mehta contributed ₹334 crore for the 8th position, Ranjan Pai entered the Top 10 with ₹219 crore, and Rohini Nilekani completed the rankings with ₹215 crore. Together, the 10 leading philanthropists donated ₹6,572 crore, representing 57% of total contributions. Concentration remains high: just 19 philanthropists donated ₹100 crore or more individually, contributing ₹7,838 crore (68% of total donations), while 125 self-made philanthropists accounted for 65% of all contributions and women increased their representation to 29 donors. Education attracted the largest contributions at ₹4,188 crore from 200 philanthropists, healthcare surged 82% to ₹1,768 crore, Mumbai contributed the highest number of philanthropists with 64 individuals (New Delhi followed with 41 and Bengaluru recorded 20), though New Delhi led in donation value at ₹3,168 crore. The findings highlight growing participation alongside continued concentration among India's biggest donors.
items.title: India's Wealthiest Donors Gave ₹11,554 Crore in FY26; Shiv Nadar Leads by a Wide Margin

items.summary: Trisha Das, a romance novelist and filmmaker, reviews Sonia Gandhi’s memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love (HarperCollins India) by treating it like a box-standard romance paperback rather than a political account. She characterizes the book as following classic romance beats—boy meets girl in Cambridge with an instant connection despite their language barrier; a tyrannical father who initially forbids the marriage until family blessing is granted; and a rushed, arranged wedding that turns ‘Happily Ever After’ into compliance, casting Sonia as the archetypal bahurani. Das concedes that later passages support genuine love: shared grief after losing their first child, Rajiv changing diapers so she could sleep, breaking barriers between her and his mother, huddling during war raids, mutual protection when a bullet was fired at them, an anniversary trip to Tehran with a self-timed photo, and Sonia’s raw grief in writing of his death. She concludes that the emotions jump off the page despite their cheesiness, though she notes the couple never aged together into old age. The piece is Das’s subjective literary framing rather than verified biographical fact; her observations are explicitly presented as interpretation drawn from the memoir's text.
items.title: Romance author frames Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi’s memoir as a conventional love story

items.summary: Guidance Tamil Nadu, the state government's investment promotion agency established in 1992 under the Industries Department, rejected media reports alleging that employees were removed for leaking sensitive information about the state's investment prospects to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh. The controversy emerged after a week following an Andhra Pradesh investment summit at which investments worth ₹10 trillion were proposed; several outlets reported that organisers of the event included former Guidance staff who had allegedly been asked to leave in July over spying allegations. It has since emerged that 13 employees resigned after serving their notice periods, while two others — Christo Laurel and Prabakaran AS — were handed relieving letters on June 29, 2026 and abruptly removed with no stated reasons; one said access was blocked within 15 minutes leaving no opportunity to back up information. Former staff denied any involvement in leaking data, describing the allegations as an attempt to deflect criticism of Tamil Nadu's comparatively weaker investment performance under the TVK government led by C Joseph Vijay. Guidance clarified that there had been no mass resignations and described attrition as a normal process while affirming healthy competition with neighbouring states; opposition leaders from DMK and AIADMK, including TRB Rajaa and Edappadi K Palaniswami, also criticised the TVK government over the episode.
items.title: Tamil Nadu's Guidance agency rejects reports of mass resignation over alleged information leak to Andhra Pradesh
