items.summary: A US congressional commission has warned that China's growing military partnership with Pakistan is increasing the risk of a two-front security challenge for India, urging Washington to deepen operational defence cooperation with New Delhi. The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission (USCC) examined this concern in a chapter titled 'China's Other Front: India and the Future of US Strategy in the Indo-Pacific,' noting that Beijing views India as one of the few countries outside the US alliance system with the demographic, economic, military, and geographic strength to challenge China long-term. The report referenced the May 2025 [d1] India-Pakistan military conflict following an Islamabad-sponsored Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people [q1], arguing it showed how China could support Pakistan during a crisis without directly entering the conflict. It highlighted India's strategic position, including its 2,100-mile contested border with China and location along key Indian Ocean sea lanes carrying significant shares of China's energy supplies and trade. The commission flagged China's expanding naval presence in the Indian Ocean as testing India's traditional advantages, recommending that Congress direct defence officials to strengthen undersea and maritime domain awareness through sustained operational coordination rather than periodic exercises. However, it cautioned that stronger India-US ties would not necessarily mean New Delhi aligns with Washington on every foreign policy objective due to its commitment to 'strategic autonomy.' The report's observations come amid efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to stabilise bilateral relations; in September, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping met at the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, expressing commitment to a fair resolution of their border dispute from a strategic perspective. A limitation is that these assessments derive from a single US congressional commission's analysis rather than independently verified data.
items.title: US report warns China-Pakistan ties raise two-front conflict risk for India

items.summary: Ukraine's President Volodymir Zelenskyy sharply rejected US President Donald Trump's characterization of Russian leader Vladimir Putin as a "friend," insisting that for Ukrainians, Putin remains an enemy and a killer who continues killing people day and night. The remarks came after Trump described his relationship with Putin as a long-standing friendship ahead of a trilateral meeting in China on Thursday with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping; Zelenskyy argued the friendly framing sends Moscow the wrong message by reducing pressure to end the war, though Trump maintains that personal ties could help conclude the conflict. Separately, Ukraine faces an intensifying winter as Russia launched its largest attack of the year: a massive overnight assault involving more than 400 drones and 110 missiles, including 27 ballistic missiles, hitting bridges in Kyiv and railway stations in western Ukraine. The strikes killed at least nine people and damaged critical infrastructure just days after Ukrainian forces badly damaged the Crimean Bridge. With temperatures falling across a country already battered by nearly five years of war, attacks on power generation facilities, electricity networks, and heating systems raise concerns that millions could be left vulnerable to freezing conditions as repair crews struggle amid continued bombardment.
items.title: Zelenskyy rebuts Trump's 'friend' label for Putin amid winter bombardment of Ukraine

items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs on Friday dismissed a United States Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF) panel as biased and politically motivated, calling its claims that India is 'targeting' Muslims during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls (SIR) unworthy of serious consideration. The rebuke came one day after USCIRF quoted its head Asif Mahmood alleging that the Indian government was removing Muslim citizens from voter rolls, labeling them as foreigners and deporting them illegally amid Home Minister Amit Shah's characterization of India's Muslims as 'infiltrators.' MEA noted the panel has a documented pattern of issuing biased assessments. The controversy centers on the SIR exercise: its first phase ran in Bihar during 2025 (d3), expanded to 12 states and Union Territories late in 2025 (d4) with a third phase covering 19 states underway, while Home Minister Shah claimed three crore voters removed were Bangladeshi infiltrators. The Opposition alleges that 13 crore (q1) voters have been intentionally deleted from the rolls where revisions occurred. In its 2026 annual report (d1), the panel recommended designating India a 'country of particular concern' for religious freedom violations, though such recommendations are non-binding. Separately, on November 14, Indian Ambassador to the US Sharjeel Imam's profile was shared by the commission; he has been imprisoned over six years since the 2020 Delhi riots conspiracy case (d2), whose trial is yet to begin. The Supreme Court upheld the legality of the revision in May but clarified that it does not authorize deciding citizenship, while BJP-ruled states have used SIR results to deny ration cards and passport renewals. Nationwide protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar began on October 2 over alleged irregularities.
items.title: MEA Rejects US Religious Freedom Panel's Allegations Against India Over Voter Roll Revision

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the newly completed Nitish Setu, a six-lane cable-stayed bridge over the River Ganga in Vaishali that connects Patna to Vaishali and is named after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. The event was framed as marking one year of the NDA government's leadership in Bihar, though it also drew political controversy because Nitish Kumar did not attend, fueling speculation amid shifting state politics; instead CM Samrat Choudhary and Union Minister Chirag Paswan were present. Alongside the bridge inauguration, Modi launched several developmental projects including 100 electric buses, highway expansions, thermal power units, and housing completions.
items.title: Modi Inaugurates Nitish Setu Bridge in Bihar

items.summary: In the first day-night Test between India and New Zealand at the Basin Reserve, KL Rahul scored his landmark 13th Test hundred (136 off 290 balls), becoming only the fourth Indian batter after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammed Azharuddin and Rahul Dravid to score a century in all of South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia. His patient innings set up skipper Shubman Gill's aggressive 98 off 146 balls before he was bowled by Jacob Duffy; the two added 100 runs for the second wicket (Rahul contributing 165 in that stand). Rishabh Pant then scored his 22nd Test half-century (55 off 62 balls), and Rahul, Gill and Pant combined to post a commanding total of 486/4 at the close of play on day three. India lead by 118 runs but would want to extend their advantage further before lunch on day four.
items.title: KL Rahul's 13th Test century paves way for India's commanding lead over New Zealand in Wellington

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the six-lane Nitish Setu bridge across the Ganga, linking Patna and Vaishali, as part of a roadshow marking one year of the NDA government. The event generated political controversy because former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar—after whom the bridge is named—did not attend despite an earlier meeting with Modi; his absence was compounded by speculation following the omission of his photograph from official advertisements and a later rally in Raja Pakar, leading opposition parties to question his declining influence. Meanwhile, Modi's roadshow featured Bihar Chief Minister Satyendra Narayan 'Samrat' Choudhary and Lok Janshakti Party leader Chirag Paswan, signaling a generational shift in state politics, and he launched infrastructure projects worth 34,000 crore rupees during the visit. The reported tensions are attributed to these circumstances rather than confirmed by independent verification of their underlying causes.
items.title: Political tension rises in Bihar after Nitish Setu inauguration by PM Modi

items.summary: PMK president Anbumani Ramadoss urged the Tamil Nadu government to declare the Cauvery delta districts as drought-affected and provide compensation of [q1: ₹40,000] (also stated as [q2: ₹40,000]) per acre to farmers whose 'Samba and Thaladi' crops were withering due to acute water scarcity. He attributed the crisis to Mettur Dam not releasing water for over a month, compounded by a Northeast Monsoon deficit, noting that discharge fell from [q4: 10,920 cusecs] on October 15 to [q5: 1,003 cusecs] on October 25. With the Mettur Dam water level at [q6: 61.53 feet] and storage at [q7: 25.84 TMC], he claimed available water could sustain supply for only about a week. He reported that crops, typically grown on over [q3: 18 lakh] acres, were restricted to around seven lakh acres this year due to anticipated shortages, with most now at the [q8: 40]-to-50-day stage and unable to survive another 70 to 80 days. Farmers reportedly spent between [q9: ₹25,000] and [q10: ₹30,000] per acre on the 'Samba' season by borrowing at high interest rates, risking an irrecoverable debt trap if crops fail. Anbumani demanded that a government team assess damage, declare the districts drought-hit, disburse relief of [q11: ₹40,000] per acre, waive land tax and levies, and grant full waivers of pending crop loans. He noted salvage would require substantial rainfall plus water release from Mettur in December and January.
items.title: PMK chief Anbumani demands Cauvery Delta drought declaration and ₹40,000 per acre relief

items.summary: Chief Minister Pema Khandu said on Saturday that Arunachal Pradesh Police has seized 18,600 kg of drugs and psychotropic substances worth around ₹75 crore since 2019. He added the force arrested 2,619 people in 1,452 registered cases over the same period while intensifying its campaign against drug trafficking. Khandu attributed part of this progress to Operation Dawn, launched in November 2023, which targeted 534 addresses and resulted in the seizure of 9,557 kg of narcotics. The remarks were made at a President's Police Colour presentation ceremony held Saturday at the Banderdewa Police Training Centre, attended by Union Home Minister Amit Shah.
items.title: Arunachal CM Khandu: Police Seized 18,600 kg of Narcotics Worth ₹75 Crore Since 2019

items.summary: Wicketkeeper Bhavika Ahire has been appointed captain of the India U-19 women's team in a five-match T20 series against England U-19, with the first match scheduled to begin November 26 in Vadodara. Seam-bowling all-rounder Anaadi Tagde is named vice-captain for the same series. The fixture serves as preparation ahead of the ICC U-19 Women's T20 World Cup set for January 2027.
items.title: Bhavika Ahire Named Captain of India U-19 Women for T20 Series vs England

items.summary: A cold wave intensified across the Nilgiris district, driving the minimum temperature in Udhagamandalam (Ooty) down to [q1: 4.4 °C] on Saturday and severely disrupting normal life. Frost concentrated during early morning hours over low-lying pockets—Kandhal, Glenmorgan, and Thalaikundha—blanketing the landscape in white. Workers at Ooty's government Botanical Garden responded by sprinkling water over lawns to melt ice layers and prevent frost damage. The temperature dip also stimulated brisk trade among roadside vendors selling woolen caps, gloves, and winter wear as residents and tourists sought protection from the chill. Despite harsh conditions, the frosted meadows attracted photographers from neighbouring Kerala and Karnataka seeking to capture the seasonal phenomenon. Ornithologists and birdwatchers additionally reported a visible increase in native Nilgiri birds and domestic migratory species gathering on the frosted grasslands for food. The report presents these observations as local accounts of an ongoing weather event, with no quantitative baseline or forecast provided beyond the single minimum-temperature reading.
items.title: Cold Wave Grips Nilgiris: Ooty Minimum Temperature Falls to 4.4°C

items.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) clarified on Saturday that permission has been granted for a Pakistani delegation to visit the Taj Mahal, while its proposed visit to the Nizamuddin Dargah in New Delhi remains without security clearance. The delegation, led by Pakistan's Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination Musadik Masood Malik, will also visit other cleared sites including Humayun's Tomb and Dilli Haat. This clarification comes as the delegation arrives in India to participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue Forum being hosted in New Delhi from November 20 to 22; Malik was received at the airport by Pakistan High Commission's Chargé d'Affaires Saad Warraich and his visit marks the first by a Pakistani minister to India in three years. The forum, inaugurated Friday evening by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, focuses on shared civilisational heritage and follows a proposal made by Modi at the SCO Summit in Tianjin, China, in 2025. The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation comprises 10 member states including India (a full member since 2017), Pakistan, China, and Russia.
items.title: MEA Clears Pakistan Delegation's Taj Mahal Visit; Withholds Clearance for Nizamuddin Dargah

items.summary: Police in Maharashtra detained eight minors following a video showing a group of boys thrashing a couple with sticks at a garden near Phoenix Mall in Kurla, Mumbai. The incident occurred on Friday, November 20, when the juveniles allegedly made lewd comments while the couple took photos; upon objection, police say the group—consisting of about eight to ten boys—physically assaulted them, beating them with sticks and chasing them down a flight of stairs. Acting on the couple's complaint, DCP Ganesh Shinde registered a case under Sections 189(2), 189(4), 118(1), 352, and 351(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). The accused are to be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board. BJP leader Kirit Somaiya identified the couple as Hindus and labeled the boys 'Muslim fanatics,' noting that notices had been served on the parents of five of them; Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Intekhab Farooqui also condemned the incident, while Bajrang Dal activists protested against the park's watchman. The report attributes Somaiya's religious characterization to him rather than presenting it as fact.
items.title: Eight boys detained after couple assaulted with sticks at Mumbai park

items.summary: Telangana Youth Congress (IYC) workers led by state president Jakkidi Shivacharan Reddy threw flower pots and damaged property at Meta's Hyderabad office on Friday, protesting restrictions imposed on the social media handles of two IYC office-bearers: national president Uday Bhanu Chib and national in-charge Manish Sharma. The protesters alleged political interference by both Meta and the BJP-led central government over accounts belonging to opposition figures such as Rahul Gandhi or posts criticising Prime Minister Modi, demanding that Meta reveal how many Indian accounts were withheld on government orders in the last six months and how many remain blocked, explain its automated blocking of certain content, remove restrictions they called unlawful against opposition voices, journalists, and creators, and respect India's constitution rather than BJP political institutions. In a post on X, the Youth Congress issued a seven-day ultimatum for Meta to "grow a spine" and restore the restricted accounts and posts, threatening escalation in courts, streets, and offices if demands were unmet. A simultaneous protest was staged by Mumbai Youth Congress president Zeenat Shabrin outside Meta's BKC office at World One, where demonstrators burnt a poster of Union Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav also criticised Meta over the restrictions on X. The BJP condemned the vandalism as proof that the Youth Congress is "a party of goons," with spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari accusing IYC workers of flaunting their destruction online, while Andhra Pradesh's BRS leader KT Rama Rao likewise branded them "goons" and questioned Rahul Gandhi over his approach to bringing companies into India. The reported restrictions on Chib and Sharma are attributed by the protesters as politically motivated but were not independently verified in the source text.
items.title: Youth Congress workers vandalise Meta office in Hyderabad over restricted accounts
